text:
mira: Heads-up — I hit a weird typing/runtime mismatch when onboarding the edge sample app with the new SDK patch. Behavior differs between ESM edge worker and local CJS node.

devon: ugh can you paste the minimal repro? is it the generic overloads we talked about?

mira: yep. minimal repro: we have a typed helper `callModel<T>(opts)` with two overloads and a generic response mapper. Works in node (CJS) but in edge runtime `T` becomes `any` in inference because of how the SDK's exported types are resolved.

samir: do you have tsconfig + package.json? most edge bundles need "module": "ES2020" or NodeNext and package.json "type":"module" or else the compiler emits different declaration shapes.

mira: package.json has "type":"module", tsconfig: `{"target":"ES2021","module":"ES2020","moduleResolution":"bundler","strict":true}` — but the SDK's declaration file uses conditional exports + `export =` fallback for CJS and that seems to confuse `tsc` in the bundler pipeline.

leo: shared note: overload resolution + generics + `export =` are fragile. TS often widens to `any` when it can't match overloads at call-site.

olivia: does the SDK expose both ESM and CJS d.ts? we recently added `types` map in package exports. could be the mapping pointing to the CJS types from the edge bundle.

mira: exact cause: rollup-style bundler used for edge sample was rewriting `import type { ModelResponse } from 'sdk'` to a generated local type alias; the generic constraint erodes at compile-time. Quick console: `// error repro\nfunction callModel<T>(opts: Options): Promise<T>;\nfunction callModel(opts: Options){ return sdk.request(opts) as any; }\n// calling site: await callModel<{id: string}>(...)` — in edge worker build the type becomes `any` at call site.

devon: failing on inference vs declaration merging. workaround: add explicit return type assertion at call site: `await callModel<{id: string}>(...) as {id: string}` — but that's not great for onboarding.

samir: alternative: make overloads non-ambiguous by having a discriminant, e.g. `callModel<T>(opts: Options & {responseType:'json'})` vs `callModel(opts: Options & {responseType:'raw'})` — then TS picks the right signature.

mira: agree, but that requires API surface change. For short-term I made a tiny patch to the edge sample bundler config: set `skipLibCheck: true` and force `preserveSymlinks: true` in rollup so dts doesn't get flattened. That fixed typing in our CI e2e.

leo: pkg-bot ran the sample test and flagged typecheck failure earlier today.

pkg-bot: typecheck: OK in node-cjs. edge-bundle: typecheck failed on master at 2587654300, passing on branch `devex/edge-typing-fix`.

olivia: can we add a short note in the onboarding README: "If using edge runtime with bundlers, prefer explicit generic usage or pin `moduleResolution` to `node`/`bundler` consistently across workspace" — most friction comes from monorepos with mixed configs.

devon: also discovered auth/retry behavior discrepancy: when the retry wrapper was typed as an overload it lost the contextual types and defaulted to `unknown` in edge builds — causing devs to sprinkle `as any` around auth logic.

mira: filed a tiny reproducer in the repo and a PR draft with two approaches: 1) change SDK overloads to use a single generic signature + discriminated union for options, 2) document bundler caveats and add CI for `tsc --build` on the edge sample.

samir: LGTM on both. For parity, let's add a CI job that runs `esbuild`/`rollup` + `tsc` on the sample so we catch these early.

leo: bonus: add a lint rule to forbid `as any` in samples so onboarding can't just hide the problem.

olivia: thanks for catching this, mira. can you drop the PR link once ready? i'll move to priority for next sprint.

mira: will do, PR incoming shortly. tl;dr: generics+overloads + conditional type exports + bundler rewrite => ambiguous inference in edge bundles; temporary workarounds, and a plan to harden SDK and sample CI. :rocket:

devon: :thumbsup:
